title: Quail Egg Canapés with Smoked Salmon, Avocado and Pickled Cucumber
summary: Pickled cucumber rounds are topped with avocado, smoked salmon and a delicate fried quail egg for an elegant, bite-sized canapé.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Pickle
steps.text: Peel the cucumber and cut 12 rounds about 5 mm thick, then toss in a bowl with 120 ml rice vinegar, ¼ tsp salt, ¼ tsp sugar and ¼ tsp chilli flakes and chill for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Drain
steps.text: Drain the cucumber rounds, pat dry and arrange on a platter.

steps.title: Top
steps.text: Mash or thinly slice half an avocado and spread over each round, then drape with the smoked salmon.

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: Melt 1 tbsp butter in a non-stick frying pan on medium, crack in 4-6 quail eggs keeping the yolks whole, and fry until the whites are set but the yolks are still soft, about 2 minutes; repeat with the remaining butter and eggs.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: Lift a fried egg onto each canapé, season with pepper and serve straight away.

tips: Pat the cucumber thoroughly dry after pickling so the toppings don't slide off.
Fry the quail eggs in small batches so each yolk stays soft and the whites don't overcook.
These runny yolks and cold-smoked salmon aren't suitable for pregnant or otherwise vulnerable guests unless the yolks are cooked until set and the salmon is hot-smoked.
storage: Best assembled and eaten immediately; the pickled cucumber alone can be chilled for up to a day before serving. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
